description:
The tool layer: resource bounds, the virtual /dev and standard streams of the embedded utilities,
and the environment and working directory they see.

cases.name: tool-layer: recursion 30 deep
cases.script: f(){ local n=$1; if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then f $((n-1)); else echo bottom; fi; }; f 30; echo status=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: recursion 60 deep
cases.script: f(){ local n=$1; if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then f $((n-1)); else echo bottom; fi; }; f 60; echo status=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: arithmetic recursion 31 deep
cases.script: f() { if (( $1 > 0 )); then f $(( $1 - 1 )); fi; }; f 31; echo status=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: fib through command substitution
cases.script: fib(){ if [ $1 -lt 2 ]; then echo $1; else echo $(( $(fib $(($1-1))) + $(fib $(($1-2))) )); fi; }; fib 14

cases.name: tool-layer: FUNCNEST
cases.script: FUNCNEST=50; f() { f; }; f; echo after $?

cases.name: tool-layer: FUNCNEST=5
cases.script: FUNCNEST=5; f() { echo $1; f $(($1+1)); echo back$1; }; f 1; echo after $?

cases.name: tool-layer: FUNCNEST in a substitution
cases.script: f() { f; }; x=$(FUNCNEST=3 f); echo st=$? x=$x; echo end

cases.name: tool-layer: arithmetic variable recursion
cases.script: a="a+1"; echo $((a)); echo after

cases.name: tool-layer: thirty nested substitutions
cases.script: echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo $(echo deep))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))

cases.name: tool-layer: tree walk 21 deep
cases.script: mkdir -p /tmp/t/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d/d; walk() { local d; for d in "$1"/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] && walk "${d%/}"; done; echo "${1#/tmp/t}"; }; walk /tmp/t | wc -l

cases.name: tool-layer: 400 nested braces

stderr.text: bash: shell code is nested too deeply for bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: nesting deeper than its WASM stacks can hold is refused (static nesting, before the script runs) or stopped with an error (recursion); bash runs until its own stack overflows and crashes

cases.name: tool-layer: endless recursion ends loudly
cases.script: f() { f; }; f; echo after

stderr.text: bash: line 1: f: maximum function nesting level exceeded (150): deeper nesting is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: nesting deeper than its WASM stacks can hold is refused (static nesting, before the script runs) or stopped with an error (recursion); bash runs until its own stack overflows and crashes

cases.name: tool-layer: command substitution over the limit
cases.script: x=$(yes | head -c 68000000); echo st=$? ${#x}; echo after

stderr.text: bash: line 1: command substitution: output over 64 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: a substitution holds at most 64 MiB in memory; past it the writer gets SIGPIPE and whoever reads the cut output gets an error

cases.script: x=$(yes | head -c 67000000); echo st=$? ${#x}

cases.script: yes | head -c 30000000 | wc -c

cases.name: tool-layer: process substitution read by head
cases.script: cat <(yes) | head -1; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: tool-layer: output process substitution
cases.script: yes > >(head -1); echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: process substitution read to the end
cases.script: cat <(yes | head -c 68000000) | wc -c; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

stderr.text: cat: /dev/fd/63: process substitution output over 64 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: a substitution holds at most 64 MiB in memory; past it the writer gets SIGPIPE and whoever reads the cut output gets an error

cases.script: cat <(yes | head -c 67000000) | wc -c; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.script: yes | head -c 50000000 > /dev/null; echo st=$?; exec 3>/dev/null; seq 3 >&3; echo st=$?

cases.script: yes | nl | head -1; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.script: yes | base64 | head -c 20; echo; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: tool-layer: endless shuf into head
cases.script: shuf -r -i 1-5 | head -3 | wc -l; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: tool-layer: piped input over the limit
cases.script: yes | head -c 68000000 | md5sum; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

stderr.text: md5sum: standard input over 64 MiB is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: an embedded utility reads at most 64 MiB of piped input before it runs (it runs synchronously); reading up to that cut is an error rather than a wrong answer

cases.name: tool-layer: piped input under the limit
cases.script: yes | head -c 67000000 | md5sum; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: tool-layer: output into a file is not limited
cases.script: yes | head -c 51000000 > /tmp/f; base64 /tmp/f > /tmp/g; wc -c < /tmp/g; base64 -d /tmp/g > /tmp/h; cmp /tmp/f /tmp/h && echo same

cases.name: tool-layer: a file operand leaves standard input alone
cases.script: echo a > /tmp/f; { nl /tmp/f; cat; } <<< data

cases.name: tool-layer: tac of a large file
cases.script: yes | head -c 50000000 > /tmp/f; echo last >> /tmp/f; tac /tmp/f | head -2; tac < /tmp/f | head -1; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: tool-layer: tac keeps records across blocks
cases.script: for n in 1 65535 65536 65537 200000; do printf '%*s\n' $n '' | tr ' ' x; done > /tmp/f; printf tail >> /tmp/f; tac /tmp/f | cksum; tac < /tmp/f | cksum

cases.name: tool-layer: sort of a file over the limit
cases.script: yes | head -c 70000000 > /tmp/f; sort /tmp/f | head -1; echo "st=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

stderr.text: sort: input over 64 MiB or 2000000 lines is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: bash-tool's limit: sort holds its input in memory on WASI (no threads for an external merge), so it refuses more than 64 MiB or 2 million lines

cases.name: tool-layer: declare -p into a pipe
cases.script: x=$(printf '%*s' 100000 ''); declare -p x | wc -c; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: tool-layer: declare -p round trip
cases.script: arr=($(seq 20000)); s=$(declare -p arr); unset arr; eval "$s"; echo ${#arr[@]}

cases.name: tool-layer: type of a large function into a pipe
cases.script: eval "big() { $(for i in $(seq 3000); do printf 'echo %s; ' $i; done) }"; type big | wc -l; declare -f big | tail -2

value.text:
cat: -: Bad file descriptor
nl: -: Bad file descriptor

expectedStderr.reason: GNU utilities report a closed standard input a second time when they close it at exit (`cat: closing standard input: …`); bash-tool reports the failed read once

cases.name: tool-layer: the program directories are not directories
cases.script: [ -d /bin ] || echo nodir; [ -x /bin ] || echo nox; [ -e /bin/cat ] || echo nofile; ls /bin > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo nolist; cd /usr/bin 2>/dev/null || echo nocd

expected.reason: bash-tool's commands run in-process and are not files: /bin/<name> runs one and -x holds for it, but /bin and /usr/bin are not directories, cannot be listed, and hold no files (-e)

cases.name: tool-layer: builtin runs only a shell builtin
cases.script: builtin env; echo st=$?; builtin cat /dev/null; echo st=$?; builtin jq -n 1; echo st=$?; builtin sh -c 'echo x'; echo st=$?; builtin timeout 1 true; echo st=$?; builtin echo hi; echo st=$?; builtin nosuch; echo st=$?; builtin type -t cat; builtin test 1 = 1 && echo t

cases.name: tool-layer: enable names only a shell builtin
cases.script: enable -n cat; echo st=$?; enable cat; echo st=$?; enable -n nosuch; echo st=$?; enable echo cat; echo st=$?; enable -n cat jq nosuch; echo st=$?

cases.script: compgen -b; compgen -A builtin c; compgen -A enabled | wc -l; compgen -A disabled | wc -l; compgen -b | grep -c -e '^cat$' -e '^jq$' -e '^timeout$'

cases.name: tool-layer: compgen -c lists this shell's commands
cases.script: compgen -c cat; compgen -c case; compgen -c jq; compgen -c timeo; compgen -c calle

cases.name: tool-layer: help knows only shell builtins
cases.script: help cat; echo st=$?; help jq sed; echo st=$?; help -s cat; echo st=$?; help -d cat; echo st=$?; help nosuch; echo st=$?; help nosuch cat; echo st=$?; help echo cat >/dev/null; echo st=$?; help -d cat echo >/dev/null; echo st=$?

cases.script: enable -p; enable | wc -l; enable -a | wc -l; enable -s; enable -p | grep -c -e ' cat$' -e ' jq$' -e ' ls$'; enable -n | wc -l

cases.script: hostname -x; echo st=$?

expected.reason: the oracle's hostname is BusyBox's (Alpine), whose usage text differs from GNU's; this shell's hostname prints the name only and refuses options it does not implement

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout stops a command
cases.script: timeout 0.3 sleep 5; echo st=$?; timeout 5 sleep 0.1; echo st=$?; timeout 0.3 bash -c 'while :; do :; done'; echo st=$?; timeout 0.3 bash -c 'while [[ 1 ]]; do x=$((x+1)); done'; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout stops a loop of pipelines
cases.script: timeout 0.3 bash -c 'while :; do echo 1 | cat >/dev/null; done'; echo st=$?; timeout 0.3 bash -c 'n=0; while :; do n=$((n+1)); echo $n | while read -r x; do :; done; done'; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout passes on the command's status and output
cases.script: timeout 1 sh -c 'exit 3'; echo st=$?; timeout 1 echo hi there; timeout 1 printf '%s\n' a b; echo in | timeout 1 cat; timeout 1 bash -c 'echo $0' x; timeout 0 sh -c 'echo ran'; echo st=$?; timeout inf true; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout signals and statuses
cases.script: timeout --preserve-status 0.3 sleep 5; echo st=$?; timeout -s INT 0.3 sleep 5; echo st=$?; timeout --signal=HUP 0.3 sleep 5; echo st=$?; timeout -s 0 0.2 sleep 1; echo st=$?; timeout -v 0.3 sleep 5; echo st=$?; timeout 1 timeout 0.2 sleep 3; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout durations
cases.script: timeout 1s true; timeout 1h true; timeout 1d true; timeout .5 true; timeout 1e0 true; echo st=$?; timeout 0.001m sleep 5; echo st=$?; timeout -- 1 true; echo st=$?

cases.name: timeout: its own errors
cases.script: timeout; echo st=$?; timeout 5; echo st=$?; timeout x sleep 1; echo st=$?; timeout -1 true; echo st=$?; timeout 1z true; echo st=$?; timeout -s FOO 1 true; echo st=$?; timeout -s 99 1 true; echo st=$?; timeout --bogus 1 true; echo st=$?; timeout -x 1 true; echo st=$?; timeout -k 1; echo st=$?; timeout --kill-after=x 1 true; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout of a command that cannot run
cases.script: timeout 1 nosuch; echo st=$?; timeout 1 /tmp; echo st=$?; timeout 1 cd /; echo st=$?; timeout 1 ./nofile; echo st=$?; f() { echo fn; }; timeout 1 f; echo st=$?; timeout 1 sleep -5; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout runs the command as a new process
cases.script: x=5; timeout 1 bash -c 'echo ${x-unset}'; export x; timeout 1 bash -c 'echo $x'; cd /tmp; timeout 1 pwd; timeout 1 xargs echo <<< 'a b'; timeout 2 true & wait $!; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout --help
cases.script: timeout --help | sed -n '1,/the exit status of COMMAND otherwise/p'; timeout --he | head -1; timeout --version >/dev/null; echo st=$?

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout that KILLs
cases.script: timeout -s KILL 0.3 sleep 5; echo st=$?

stderr.text: bash: line 1:     2 Killed                     timeout -s KILL 0.3 sleep 5

expected.reason: bash names the process KILL ended; process numbers here count from the call's own, so timeout's child is 2 where the oracle's is a system pid

cases.name: tool-layer: timeout of a shell with its own TERM handling
cases.script: timeout 0.3 sh -c 'trap "echo caught; exit 5" TERM; while :; do :; done'; echo st=$?; timeout -k 0.3 0.3 sh -c 'trap "" TERM; sleep 5'; echo st=$?

expected.reason: limit: `sh` and `bash` here run inside timeout's child process rather than replacing it (no exec), so the signal that ends the child ends the nested shell with it: a TERM trap or ignored TERM in a nested shell does not run or hold; the call's own TERM trap does
